question: Can the verified ARCore pose-diverse selector be attached to the current default-App camera path without losing exact source-frame pose authority or changing user guidance?

current_camera_source.observed_contract: CameraX Preview plus 640x480 RGBA ImageAnalysis, KEEP_ONLY_LATEST at requested 24 fps; emits Camera2 timestamp FrameStamp and no VIO or Anchor pose.

vision_frame_contract.observed_contract: Carries frame identity, optional ranging and transport timing; no source-frame camera pose receipt.

frame_processor.observed_contract: Consumes one current VisionFrame, runs the production detector, then commits risk/rendering under one lifecycle lease.

runtime_controller.observed_contract: Creates the CameraX phone source through FrameSourceFactory; no ARCore session or spatial source selection exists.

phone_preview.observed_contract: PHONE_CAMERA provides CameraX PreviewView; no generic Camera2 or ARCore Surface host is exposed.

external_primary_sources.title: Shared camera access with ARCore
external_primary_sources.used_for: SharedCamera requires Session.Feature.SHARED_CAMERA, Camera2 wrapped callbacks and explicit app surfaces; extra surfaces increase device performance demand.

external_primary_sources.title: ARCore SharedCamera reference
external_primary_sources.used_for: SharedCamera shares CameraDevice and CameraCaptureSession state with ARCore; app-created surfaces are device-dependent and ARCore depth is unavailable in shared-camera mode.

external_primary_sources.title: CameraX architecture
external_primary_sources.used_for: CameraX owns lifecycle-bound Preview and ImageAnalysis use cases; stream combinations and processing demand vary by device.

reasons: No ARCore Frame or Anchor-relative pose is present on the emitted VisionFrame.
Camera2 image timestamp alone cannot reconstruct ARCore translation or the frozen selector's same-world-frame invariant.
Opening a separate exclusive ARCore Session beside the existing CameraX provider risks camera ownership conflict and does not establish exact shared-frame identity.
PreviewView is bound to CameraX rather than exposed as a generic SharedCamera Camera2 Surface.
It is the documented path for concurrent app-owned Camera2 surfaces and ARCore tracking.
A custom YUV ImageReader timestamp can be compared exactly with ARCore Frame.timestamp without nearest fallback.
It tests the missing product-source seam while keeping detector, risk, feedback and default App unchanged.

frozen_source_canary.question: On the current SM-S9280, can ARCore SharedCamera and one app-owned 640x480 YUV_420_888 ImageReader produce exact timestamp-bound CPU payload and Anchor-relative pose receipts that support the frozen pose-diverse selector?
frozen_source_canary.camera_api: Camera2 with ARCore-wrapped device and session callbacks
frozen_source_canary.app_surface: one 640x480 YUV_420_888 ImageReader surface registered through SharedCamera.setAppSurfaces
frozen_source_canary.frame_identity: Image.timestamp must equal ARCore Frame.timestamp exactly; no nearest-timestamp, frame-id-only or cross-epoch fallback
frozen_source_canary.pose_identity: Anchor-relative UstrfPoseSample timestamp and camera frame must match the exact source frame

claim_ceiling: This audit rejects only direct attachment to the current CameraX analyzer because it lacks exact ARCore pose authority. A future SharedCamera source-canary PASS would establish only one-device app-owned CPU-frame plus ARCore-pose source feasibility, not detector accuracy, App integration, thermal stability, product effectiveness or safety.
